newsitem.title: USA: SEC sues New York investment newsletter publisher.
newsitem.headline: SEC sues New York investment newsletter publisher.

text.p: The Securites and Exchange Commission said Friday it sued the publisher of a New York-based investment newsletter for alleged stock manipulation that cost investors more than $1.5 million.

In a civil complaint filed on Thursday in U.S. District Court in Manhattan, the SEC alleged the publisher and two of its principals defrauded investors of at least $1.5 million through the sale of American Image Motor Co. Inc. stock.

Named in the complaint were Global Financial Traders Ltd, publisher of the Daily Speculator; its affiliate BGSG Holdings Corp; Michael Reilly, 35, of Dix Hills, N.Y., an officer of BGSG and a principal of Global; and John Kenna, 28, of Long Beach, N.Y., also an officer of BGSG and a principal of Global.
Global and BGSG are controlled by Reilly and Kenna, the commission said.
The attorney for Global Financial, Franklin Ormsten, based in Jericho, N.Y., did not return a phone call for comment.

In the complaint, the SEC alleged Reilly and Kenna made statements in the Daily Speculator recommending subscribers buy shares of American Image without telling them they held about 46 percent of American's unrestricted stock.

SEC alleged Reilly and Kenna sold American Image stock to the public, especially to subscribers in the newsletter, while manipulating the market of American Image by secretly bidding for and purchasing the stock.
Reilly, Kenna, Global and BGSG failed to tell investors they control distribution and trading by the largest market maker for American Image, the agency charged.

Also named in the complaint were Vincent Iovine, 35, of Nesconset, N.Y., a registered representative and head trader at Northeast Securities since May 1992; and David Coleman, 45, of Phoeniz, Ariz., a registered representative and trader employed by Wilson-Davis & Co.
Ivoine and Coleman both effected large transactions in American Image, the commission said.
Trading at both Northeast and Wilson-Davis has been primarily for a handful of related customer accounts controlled by and whose beneficial owners are Reilly and Kenna, the regulatory agency said.
American Image Motor, based in Santa Cruz, Calif., is purportedly a manufacturer of high-end motorcyles designed to compete with those manufactured by Harley-Davidson Inc, the SEC said.
American Image started trading on the Over the Counter Bulletin Board in August 1996.

The commission said it is seeking to enjoin them from future violations of federal securities laws, payment of ill-gotten gains plus prejudgment interest and civil penalties from each of the defendants.
